The LTD command is also used to transfer horizontal loads from the source system by speci- fying LTD DIR X and/or Y. The following two special features apply:
 • Constant load distribution: Regardless of the selected load transfer functions (see sec- tion: 9.2), horizontal loads are always transferred as a constant distribution. The torsional moment around the vertical building axis is not taken into account.
 • Bending moments from horizontal loads: In contrast to the torsional moment, it is possi- ble to transfer bending moments resulting from horizontal loads and the storey height. The table defines the input parameters (Items) for the LTD (Load Take Down) command, with four columns:  
• Item – the keyword used in the input file.  
• Description – a brief summary of the parameter’s role.  
• Unit – the expected data type or unit.  
• Default – the value assumed if the parameter is omitted.  

1. OPT  
   – Unit: LIT4 (4-character literal)  
   – Default: TASK  
   – Description: Determines the record’s function within a load-take-down procedure. It must be one of:  
     • TASK – begins a new load-take-down task (creates or switches a target load case).  
     • SEL  – supplementary record to select additional source or target geometries.  
     • IGN  – supplementary record to exclude previously selected geometries.  
     • MOD  – supplementary record to modify a mapping, effectively an IGN + new TASK for a single source→target reassignment.  

2. SRLC  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: (required, indicated by “!”)  
   – Description: The load-case ID in the source database whose loads are to be transferred.  

3. SRCT  
   – Unit: LIT4  
   – Default: ALL  
   – Description: Specifies which type of source geometries to include:  
     • SLN  – structural lines (e.g. walls)  
     • SPT  – structural points (e.g. columns)  
     • GRP  – a predefined group of elements  
     • GUID – geometries identified by GUID  
     • ALL  – all SLNs and SPTs  

4. SRC  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: –  
   – Description: A comma-separated list of IDs or GUIDs identifying the source geometries selected by SRCT. Mandatory unless SRCT=ALL.  

5. TRGT  
   – Unit: LIT4  
   – Default: AUTO  
   – Description: Specifies how target geometries are determined:  
     • SLN/SPT/GRP – explicitly assign by structural line/point numbers or group  
     • AUTO  – automatically find geometries matching source floor plan  
     • FALL  – “falldown” mode: duplicate the load-bearing source geometries as targets  

6. TRG  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: –  
   – Description: A comma-separated list of target IDs (SLN/SPT or group). Mandatory unless TRGT=AUTO or FALL.  

7. LMAX  
   – Unit: [m]  
   – Default: 0.0  
   – Description: Maximum subdivision length for target geometries. If 0.0, subdivision is deactivated (no splitting of lines).  

8. TRGM  
   – Unit: LIT4  
   – Default: INDI  
   – Description: Mode for distributing loads among multiple target geometries:  
     • INDI – each target picks up loads nearest it, individually distributing forces and moments  
     • COMB – all targets act as a stiff unit; source loads are summed into a resultant and shared  

9. DZ  
   – Unit: –  
   – Default: 0.0  
   – Description: Z-offset (storey height) applied in FALL mode, i.e. the vertical drop distance for duplicated geometries.  

10. TYPE  
    – Unit: LIT4  
    – Default: CONS  
    – Description: Defines how source loads are transmitted to the target:  
      • CONS – constant line loads; preserves resultant forces (but not moments) evenly  
      • MOMT – trapezoidal loads; preserves both force and moment resultants (if targets can resist moment)  
      • TRAP – positive trapezoidal; geometric placement of the resultant force, ensures no uplift, preserves forces only  

11. FACT  
    – Unit: –  
    – Default: 1.0  
    – Description: Uniform multiplier applied to all transferred loads (e.g. use FACT=–1.0 to invert load direction).  

Together, these parameters control selection, mapping, geometric treatment, load transmission law, and scaling of loads when importing support reactions from a “source” database into a “target” model.

Below is a field-by-field breakdown of the “LTD” input table.  This description covers the purpose of each parameter, its format, default value (where defined) and any special notes or dependencies.  Use this as a guide when parsing or generating LTD records for your RAG vector store.

1.  SRLC  
    •  Type: Integer  
    •  Description: Reference ID of the new load-take-down record (equivalent to “load case”).  
    •  Default: none (mandatory)  
    •  Notes: All LTD entries use this SRLC to group loads.

2.  FACT  
    •  Type: Real scalar  
    •  Description: Overall multiplier applied to every transferred load.  
    •  Default: 1.0  
    •  Format: “FACT <value>” where <value> is a signed float.  
    •  Notes: Negative values invert load direction.

3.  FROM  
    •  Type: Quoted string  
    •  Description: Path/name of the source database (CDB) from which loads are taken.  
    •  Default: none (mandatory)  
    •  Format: FROM "<filename.cdb>"

4.  SRCT / SRC  
    •  SRCT Type: Keyword to specify source-geometry selection mode.  
         – Allowed values: SLN (structural line), SPT (structural point), GRP (group), GUID (source only), ALL.  
    •  SRC   Type: Comma-separated list of IDs or GUIDs (if SRCT=GUID).  
    •  Description: Defines which source elements’ loads to import.  
    •  Default: none (mandatory if not using SRCT ALL)  
    •  Notes: Must precede any MOD or IGN that refer to source items.

5.  TRGT / TRG  
    •  TRGT Type: Keyword to specify target-geometry selection mode.  
         – Allowed values: SLN, SPT, GRP, AUTO, FALL.  
    •  TRG  Type: Comma-separated list of target IDs (for SLN/SPT/GRP modes).  
    •  Description: Defines where to apply the imported loads in the current model.  
    •  Default: none (mandatory unless TRGT is AUTO or FALL)  
    •  Notes:  
         – AUTO attempts an automatic SLN/SPT match (floor plans must be very similar).  
         – FALL duplicates each source element at its original location (“fall-down”).  

6.  OPT  
    •  Type: Flag indicating use of selection modifiers.  
    •  Description: Signals that subsequent SEL, IGN or MOD commands refine the source/target sets.  
    •  Notes: OPT itself carries no arguments; it simply introduces the selection stage.

7.  SEL  
    •  Type: “SEL SRCT|TRGT <mode> <keyword> <list>”  
    •  Description: Add source or target geometries to the selection.  
    •  Notes: Can be called multiple times to accumulate selections.

8.  IGN  
    •  Type: “IGN SRCT|TRGT <mode> <keyword> <list>”  
    •  Description: Remove geometries from the current source/target set.  
    •  Notes: Used primarily after SRCT ALL or AUTO to prune mis-matches.  Can only remove a source load if it isn’t shared by other SLNs/SPTs still in the set.

9.  MOD  
    •  Type: “MOD SRCT SLN SRC <id> TRGT SPT TRG <id>”  
    •  Description: Short-cut for ignoring a wrong automatic match and then explicitly re-tasking that load onto the correct target.  
    •  Notes: Only the specified source is removed; other source → target mappings remain intact.

10.  TRGM  
    •  Type: Keyword  
    •  Allowed values: INDI, COMB  
    •  Description: Target‐model strategy  
         – INDI (individual): Each target geometry receives loads based on its own nearest source loads.  
         – COMB (combined): All source loads are summed, then distributed to all targets as a single cross-section.  
    •  Default: INDI

11.  TYPE  
    •  Type: Keyword  
    •  Allowed values: CONS, MOMT, TRAP  
    •  Description: Load distribution rule  
         – CONS: Constant line loads; conserves total force only.  
         – MOMT: Trapezoidal line loads; conserves force and moment (if targets can resist moment).  
         – TRAP: Positive trapezoidal (no uplifting segments; conserves force only).  
    •  Default: CONS  
    •  Notes: Point-only elements (columns) assume an equivalent length (0.5 m) and cannot transfer moments.

12.  DIR  
    •  Type: Keyword or combination (X, Y, Z, XY, XZ, YZ, XYZ)  
    •  Description: Which load components to transfer  
    •  Default: XYZ  
    •  Notes: E.g. “DIR XY” transfers all horizontal forces.

13.  HMOM  
    •  Type: Keyword or real  
    •  Allowed values: OFF, AUTO, <height>[unit]  
    •  Description: Controls transfer of story-height moments generated by horizontal forces  
         – OFF: Disable  
         – AUTO: Height = mean distance between source & target geometries  
         – explicit: User-defined height value (e.g. “5[m]”)  
    •  Default: OFF  
    •  Preconditions: DIR must include X or Y, and TYPE must be MOMT.

––––  
In practice, an LTD command sequence starts with SRLC and FROM, then optionally FACT, TRGM, TYPE, DIR, HMOM.  If specific geometry selection is required, add “LTD OPT” followed by any combination of SEL, IGN or MOD statements to tailor the source and target sets before concluding the load-take-down.

The table excerpt shown here defines three of the key options available when you invoke an LTD (Load Take Down) operation in your FEM-processing workflow.  Each row of the table names one parameter (Item), explains its purpose and the allowable values (Description), indicates the syntax or unit token expected in the input (Unit), and finally gives the default if you do not explicitly supply a value (Default).  Below is a detailed breakdown of each:

1.  DIR  
    •  Purpose: Specifies which component(s) of the support forces are to be transferred from source to target geometries.  In other words, it controls the direction(s) of the “Dropped-down” loads.  
    •  Allowed literals:  
       –  X  – transfers only the global-X force components  
       –  Y  – transfers only the global-Y force components  
       –  Z  – transfers only the global-Z (vertical) force components  
       You may combine them (e.g. “DIR XY” to move only horizontal forces, or “DIR XYZ” for all three).  
    •  Unit token:  LIT   (this simply denotes that you must supply one or more literal letters)  
    •  Default:  Z  (if you omit DIR, only vertical support forces are taken down)

2.  HMOM  
    •  Purpose: Governs whether bending moments—generated by the horizontal force components over the story height—are also transferred along with the pure forces.  This is only meaningful when you have chosen to transfer horizontal forces (i.e. DIR X, DIR Y or DIR XY) *and* you are using a transfer function that can carry moments (TYPE MOMT).  
    •  Allowed values:  
       –  OFF   – moment transfer is deactivated (only forces go across)  
       –  AUTO  – the “story height” is computed automatically from the average vertical distance between corresponding source and target geometry.  (Alternatively, you may override AUTO by specifying an explicit height on the command line, e.g. “HMOM 5[m].”)  
    •  Unit token:  LIT4/–   (indicates a literal string or an optional numeric height with units)  
    •  Default:  OFF

3.  FROM  
    •  Purpose: Points the LTD command at the source database from which the loads are to be read.  This is the filename (and optional path) of the CDB (or other supported) file that contains the line- and point-load definitions you want to import.  
    •  Unit token:  LIT   (you must provide a literal text string, typically in quotes, e.g. `"source.cdb"`)  
    •  Default:  “!”  (there is no implicit source database; you must supply this)

How these options fit into the overall LTD workflow:  
-  Every LTD invocation begins with declaring or referencing a load case (via LC or an earlier TASK).  
-  FROM is mandatory: without it, no source loads can be located.  
-  DIR allows you to filter whether you take down only vertical loads (the default), only horizontal, or any combination.  
-  HMOM refines that behavior by choosing whether the resulting bending moments (due to horizontal forces acting over a height) should also be carried into the new model.  If you leave HMOM OFF, only pure forces will appear in the target.  If you choose AUTO (or specify a height), the software computes or uses that height to turn horizontal-force pairs into equivalent bending moments.  

In practice, a minimal command to drop only vertical forces from “source.cdb” into your current model might look like:  
   LTD SRLC 1 DIR Z FROM "source.cdb"  

If instead you wanted to carry through both X­- and Y-forces and also include the induced bending moments over a 4 m story height, you would write:  
   LTD SRLC 1 DIR XY HMOM 4[m] FROM "source.cdb"

See also: LC, LTDG

 The LTD command can be used to apply the load from a source database to the current model as line and point loads.
 Note: The LTD record must follow a LC set: LC creates a new load case in the current target database to which the loads are assigned.
 TASK creates a new load take down. After a LTD TASK, any number of LTD SEL/- MOD/IGN records can follow. Here, only the inputs SRCT, SRC, TRGT, TRG are interpreted. All other information is taken from the preceding TASK record.
 OPT
 SEL can be used to select multiple source and/or target geometries.
 LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 FROM "source.cdb" LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 201,202,203 LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN TRG 101,102,103
 IGN can be used to remove source/target geometries from the selection.
 MOD With MOD, an 1:1 assignment can be created within a TASK. The intended application scenario is: With SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO, all loads are auto- matically transferred to the target geometries. At some locations a wrong target geometry is identified. In this case, with MOD the loads can be ’cut out’ and applied directly to the assigned target geometry. MOD is thus a short command for an LTD IGN followed by an LTD TASK:
 $ All source loads are automatically distributed However, the
 load from SLN 201 is misallocated. SPT 103 would be correct LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO FROM "source.cdb" LTD OPT MOD SRCT SLN SRC 201 TRGT SPT TRG 103
 $ is equivalent to:
 LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO FROM "source.cdb"
 LTD OPT IGN SRCT SLN SRC 201
 LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 FROM "source.cdb"

SPT 103 would be correct LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO FROM "source.cdb" LTD OPT MOD SRCT SLN SRC 201 TRGT SPT TRG 103. $ is equivalent to:. LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO FROM "source.cdb". LTD OPT IGN SRCT SLN SRC 201. LTD OPT TASK SRLC 1 FROM "source.cdb".
 LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 201
 LTD OPT SEL TRGT SPT TRG 103
 Note: For MOD, only the source geometry is removed/ignored, as other loads may need the same target geometry for load take down.
 Note: With MOD and IGN, source geometries and thus support loads are removed from the selection. However, these loads can only be removed if they are only associated with a single SLN or if all corresponding SLNs are removed.
 SRC/TRG If a structural element (SLN/SPT), group or GUID (only for source) is requested by SRCT/TRGT, an input for the desired items is mandatory.
 There are three ways to choose target geometries:
 SLN/SPT/GRP The number of the type of geometry or group.
 AUTO It is tried to select from all existing structural lines (SLN) and points (SPT) those that could be walls or columns. This method should only be used if the source and destination floor plan are very similar. Note: Structure lines and points have no information about whether they are actually walls or columns, which can lead to incorrect associations. A verification of the applied loads is therefore imperative.
 Falldown: All load-bearing source geometries are duplicated. Note: The target geometry is not analysed. With different floor plans (e.g. openings) it can happen that loads can not be applied correctly.
 FALL
 There are two ways to model the target geometries:
 Individual: Each structure line and point will find the nearest source loads and form the resulting load distribution according to the selected type TYPE.
 INDI
 COMB Combined: All target geometries are considered as one unit. All source loads form a total resultant and are distributed to all target geometries according to the selected type TYPE. This can be used to model the stiff connection of target geometries, such as for a stiffening building core.
 TYPE There are three ways to transfer the loads:
 CONS Constant line loads. The resultant from the support forces of the source geometries is distributed constantly to all target geometries. The sum of forces is conserved.

This can be used to model the stiff connection of target geometries, such as for a stiffening building core.. TYPE There are three ways to transfer the loads:. CONS Constant line loads. The resultant from the support forces of the source geometries is distributed constantly to all target geometries. The sum of forces is conserved..
 MOMT Trapezoidal line loads. The resulting force and moment(s) are represented by trapezoidal line loads. The sum of forces and moments is conserved (sum of moments only if the target geometries are able to take the mo- ment).
 TRAP Positive trapezoidal line loads. The position of the resultant force de- termines the trapezoidal load purely geometrically. In extreme cases — when the resultant is outside the target geometry — a triangular load is created. This type of distribution prevents lifting forces, an models an in- fluence of the moment. However, only the sum of the forces and not the moments are conserved.
 Note: For columns, an equivalent length of 0.5m is assumed. Columns can only transfer point forces. Hence, columns that act individually (see TRGM INDI/COMB) are not able to transfer moments.
 DIR determines the direction of the loads to be transferred. Multiple selection is possible, e.g. all loads: DIR XYZ or all horizontal loads: DIR XY.
 HMOM de/activates the transfer from moments that are generated from horizontal forces over the storey height (see section 9.4). In order for the moment to be transferred:
 •
 the transmission of horizontal forces must be activated: DIR X, DIR Y, or DIR XY and
 • TYPE MOMT must be selected as transfer function.
 The following options are available:
 Deactivates bending moments from horizontal forces.
 AUTO The height is calculated as the mean distance between the source and target geometry.
 explicit The height can be specified explicitly by the user.
 $ Loads from structural line 201 are transferred to structural line 101 LTD SRLC 1 SRCT SLN SRC 201 TRGT SLN TRG 101 FROM "source.cdb"
 $ Loads from structural lines 201,202 are transferred to structural lines
 101,102,103
 LTD SRLC 1 FROM "source.cdb" LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 201,202 $ sources LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN SRC 101,102,103 $ targets

$ Loads from structural lines 201,202 are transferred to structural lines. 101,102,103. LTD SRLC 1 FROM "source.cdb" LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 201,202 $ sources LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN SRC 101,102,103 $ targets.
 $ All source loads will be automatically distributed
 LTD SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO FROM "source.cdb"
 $ All source geometries fall down
 LTD SRLC 1 SRCT ALL TRGT FALL FROM "source.cdb"
 $ Modelling of a stiffening building core with 4 walls
 $ Modelling of a stiffening building core with 4 walls
 $ - Source: Support loads from structural lines 201,202,203,204
 $ - Source: Support loads from structural lines 201, 202,203,204
 $ - Target: Structural lines 101,102,103,104
 $ - Sum of forces and moments at the summarised target "cross section"
 LTD SRLC 1 TYPE MOMT TRGM COMB FROM "source.cdb"
 LTD OPT SEL SRCT SLN SRC 201,202,203,204
 LTD OPT SEL TRGT SLN TRG 101,102,103,104
 $ Transfer of horizontal loads and resulting bending moments
 LTD SRLC 2 SRCT ALL TRGT AUTO TYPE MOMT DIR XY HMOM 5[m] FROM "source.cdb"

The table shown defines the schema for all coordinate and metadata fields that the LTDG command accepts when you build points, lines or arcs under an SRLC import task.  It consists of four columns—Item, Description, Unit and Default—and nine rows of actual data fields plus two metadata rows (TITLE and GUID).  Below is a breakdown of every column and row, together with how each field is used in the context of point, line or arc creation.

1. Columns  
   • Item – the internal parameter name used by the LTDG routine.  
   • Description – a human‐readable explanation of each parameter.  
   • Unit – the data type or unit in which the field is expressed.  Coordinates are in metres; text fields use literal string types.  
   • Default – a one‐character flag that indicates whether a field is mandatory or optional in different geometries:  
     – “!” means always required (for single point or as start-point of line/arc)  
     – “*” means optional (required only if you are defining a second point or an arc midpoint)  
     – “–” means not used for geometry (meta only)

2. Coordinate Groups  
   a) Start-point coordinates (P1)  
     • X1 (X-coordinate of the start point)  
     • Y1 (Y-coordinate of the start point)  
     • Z1 (Z-coordinate of the start point)  
     Unit: [m]₁₀₀₁  
     Default: “!” – always required for any geometry.  If you supply one of these you must supply all three together.  

   b) Secondary-point coordinates (P2)  
     • X2 (X-coordinate of the point)  
     • Y2 (Y-coordinate of the point)  
     • Z2 (Z-coordinate of the point)  
     Unit: [m]₁₀₀₁  
     Default: “*” – required only when defining a line or an arc.  Not used for single‐point input.  

   c) Third-point or arc-midpoint coordinates (P3)  
     • X3 (X-coordinate of a circle point)  
     • Y3 (Y-coordinate of a circle point)  
     • Z3 (Z-coordinate of a circle point)  
     Unit: [m]₁₀₀₁  
     Default: “*” – required only when defining an arc.  This point must lie between P1 and P2 on the intended circle.  

3. Metadata Fields  
   • TITL – free‐form Title.  Unit: LIT12 (a 12-character text literal).  
     Default: “–” (not part of the geometric definition).  

   • GUID – Globally Unique Identifier.  Unit: LIT36 (a 36-character UUID string).  
     Default: “–”  

4. How It All Works in Practice  
   – For a single point: supply X1,Y1,Z1 (“!” fields) only.  
   – For a line: supply X1,Y1,Z1 and X2,Y2,Z2.  The “*” fields X2/Y2/Z2 become mandatory.  
   – For an arc: supply all nine coordinates X1–Z1, X2–Z2 and X3–Z3.  The intermediate P3 point determines the curvature; the system automatically segments the arc into straight segments.  If you need finer segmentation, set LMAX in your preceding LTD OPT TASK.  

By following this schema, the vector‐import routine unambiguously knows which points define the start and end of lines, and how to interpolate true arcs when the third point is provided.

 LTDG
 The LTDG command can be used to directly create points, lines and arcs for the target geome- tries. The LTDG command must follow a LTD OPT TASK. LTDG can be called several times and then adds more target geometries to the task (analogous to LTD OPT SEL).
 Note: If a coordinate x, y, z of a point is set, the remaining two must be specified as well.
 For the input of a point, only the coordinates for P1(1,y1,z1) are to be given.
 Lines: To enter a line, enter the coordinates for the starting point P1(1,y1,z1) and the ending point P2(2,y2,z2).
 Arcs: To enter an arc, all points must be specified. Note that the point P3(3,y3,z3) lies between the start and end point on the arc. The arc is automatically divided into line segments. If the subdivision is too coarse, it can be controlled in the preceding TASK with the LMAX command.
 LTD SRLC 1
 FROM "source.cdb"
 SRCT SLN SRC 201 $ Choose source LTDG X1 1 2 3 LTDG X1 0 0 0 x2 10 0 0 $ Choose target-line LTDG X1 0 0 0 x2 10 0 0 x3 5 1 0 $ Choose target-arc
 LTD SRLC 1. FROM "source.cdb”
 $ Choose target-point
